firstRoundFindings: quiz.q9: Correct the explanations for options 2 and 3 (zero-based). After incorrectly rewriting the integrand as $e^{2x/5}$, correct integration gives option 3, $\frac52e^{2x/5}+C$, so its explanation must name only the incorrect root rewrite; option 2 additionally divides by the original coefficient $5/2$ instead of the rewritten coefficient $2/5$. The answers and correct-option flag remain valid.

quiz.dq-3504: Options 1 and 2 (zero-based) have explanations that only reject the answers rather than name specific mistakes. Identify option 1's misuse of the power-function differentiation pattern on $e^x$, and option 2's misuse of the power-integration pattern by increasing the exponent and dividing by that exponent.

theory: The procedure says every term becomes a power of $e$ and then instructs division by its index coefficient, but expansion can produce constant terms with coefficient $a=0$. Explicitly distinguish exponential terms with nonzero linear index coefficient from constant terms, which integrate to the constant times $x$; otherwise the procedure implies division by zero for several supplied items.
summary: Corrected the specified distractor explanations in quiz.q9 and quiz.dq-3504 to name the exact mistakes. Clarified the theory text and procedure so division applies only when the linear index coefficient is nonzero and constant terms integrate to the constant times $x$; no whole items were removed.
reviewSummary: All eight scoped items have correct answers, usable working and booklet-supported question types within the target skill. The theory matches the taught method, and each reviewed quiz has exactly one correct option with accurate distractor explanations.
